title: The record collection he lost in Louisville
summary: He kept his Buffalo record collection but lost his earliest ones (Armstrong, Red Nichols with Rollini, Teagarden) because he moved from room to room and his mother discarded them.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Listen, Jonah, do you mean that you collected these and you've still got all the records you were buying in those days?
You kept them with you. You never --
I'm so sorry that I missed those in Kentucky, because after I left, you know, I guess my mother must have just thrown them away, or they got broke or something.
That you first had, you mean?

Yeah, that I first had, with Louis Armstrong and Red Nichols playing "Indiana," "Back Home in Indiana," and Adrian Rollini and all them guys, you know. A pretty nice thing. And Teagarden playing things like, "Dinah," and all that stuff. I had all that stuff back there in Louisville you know. But -- and I left, and naturally I had forgotten all about them myself. Other things were happening. And living from room to room, you know.
Yeah, going from place to place.
